I also refactored the loop logic to use these helpers, and updated the task‑prompt builder to accept a specific task and optional feedback. Consequently, the existing unit tests for the prompt‑building utilities are now out‑of‑date—they still only check that the generic plan and loop prompts contain the goal and a few hard‑coded strings. def test_prompts_contain_goal_and_contract() -> None:
    goal = "verify tests work"
    task = "- [ ] write tokenizer — implement bpe merges"
    plan_prompt = ralph.build_plan_prompt(goal)
    task_prompt = ralph.build_task_prompt(goal, task, None)
    verify_prompt = ralph.build_verify_prompt(task)
    assert goal in plan_prompt
    assert "ralph/tasks.md" in plan_prompt
    assert "- [ ]" in plan_prompt
    assert goal in task_prompt
    assert task in task_prompt
    assert "read AGENTS.md completely" in task_prompt
    assert "journal.md" in task_prompt
    assert "docs/functions.md" in task_prompt
    assert task in verify_prompt
    assert ralph.VERIFIED_SENTINEL in verify_prompt
    assert ralph.INCOMPLETE_SENTINEL in verify_prompt


def test_task_prompt_with_feedback_tells_agent_to_continue() -> None:
    goal = "verify tests work"
    task = "- [ ] write tokenizer — implement bpe merges"
    feedback = "RALPH_INCOMPLETE: encode works but decode was never implemented"
    prompt = ralph.build_task_prompt(goal, task, feedback)
    assert "Continue from where it left off" in prompt
    assert feedback in prompt
